seoTitle: Puerto Rico Law 75: dealer changes, termination and nonrenewal
title: Puerto Rico Law 75: check the dealer relationship before changing the deal
description: Understand the reviewed Law 75 dealer responsibilities and change questions; keep the 2020 source limit, later-law gaps and arbitration qualifications visible.

sections.heading: Look at the job the local party has undertaken
paragraphs: The official Spanish consolidation of Law 75 defines the relationship by what the parties have actually established. Its definition includes taking real responsibility for distributing goods or providing services by concession or franchise in the Puerto Rico market. The first task is therefore to describe that responsibility, rather than relying on the agreement’s title.

Who develops customers, carries stock, provides service, hires local staff and invests in the market? Those facts help frame whether the particular relationship falls within the law. This guide does not conclude that every franchise, distributor or service partner is a protected dealer.

sections.heading: Why an expiry date or exit clause may not settle the decision
paragraphs: In the reviewed text, Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, even where the contract reserves unilateral exit. A fixed term or an express right to end the contract therefore should not be treated as the entire analysis. Article 2A also contains specific presumptions and qualifications about impairment.

That does not make every change unlawful. It means the proposed action, legal conditions and evidence must be examined together before a notice is sent. Likewise, statutory factors for damages are not a ready-made forecast or an automatic refund of everything the partner has spent.

sections.heading: Worked example: taking the largest account back
paragraphs: Fictional example. A European industrial-maintenance brand appoints a Puerto Rico partner to develop customers, employ technicians and support installed equipment. After two years, the brand wants to serve the largest customer directly. Finance sees a simple way to keep more revenue and asks operations to reassign the account.

The local partner may have built that account and organised staff around it. Removing the account could therefore raise a relationship question rather than merely change an internal sales allocation. Before acting, the COO gathers the existing account terms, who won the customer, who delivers and funds service, performance records and the exact proposed change. The relevant review then tests dealer status, any impairment provision and justification. The example explains why evidence is needed; it does not decide that the account is protected or that damages are due.

sections.heading: Try the decision: can the brand take the account back?
paragraphs: Use the fictional industrial-maintenance example above. Before reading the answer, choose the evidence that matters: the agreement’s label, who developed the customer, who funded and organised service, or the exact change proposed. Does an expiry date or a reserved direct-sales clause alone settle the result?

Answer: the actual relationship and proposed action need to be examined together. In the Spanish consolidation revised on 13 November 2020, the Law 75 definition concerns real responsibility for distributing goods or providing services by concession or franchise in Puerto Rico. Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, while Article 2A has its own presumptions and qualifications. A reserved account and an account developed by the local party therefore belong in separate factual enquiries; neither label alone establishes protection or permission to remove it.

The useful next step is to gather the signed terms, customer-development and service history, investment, performance concerns and proposed notice. This is not a finding that the fictional account is protected or that damages are owed. The reviewed Spanish consolidation was revised on 13 November 2020; later amendments, controlling cases and the federal-law interaction with forum/arbitration wording remain unresolved.

sections.heading: Prepare a change file before making a promise
paragraphs: Keep the signed agreement and proposed notice with a factual history of market development, service, investment, quality complaints and any opportunity to correct performance. Identify reserved accounts, direct-sales rights and exclusivity separately. Ask which legal conditions and current cases apply to this specific proposed appointment, change, nonrenewal or termination.

The reviewed government consolidation is in Spanish and was revised on 13 November 2020. This English explanation is AI-assisted, not an official translation. Later amendments and controlling cases remain to be checked. Its forum and arbitration wording also needs assessment against applicable federal law; this page does not say every arbitration clause outside Puerto Rico is invalid.

sections.heading: Other approvals remain separate
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule includes a franchise located in a U.S. territory, subject to its exemptions. That does not decide independent territorial sales duties or this dealer-law question. Puerto Rico is inside the defined U.S. customs territory, but that boundary fact does not establish local taxes, a product’s classification or origin. Company, premises, staff and immigration questions need their own records.

seoTitle: U.S. Virgin Islands business licences: DLCA and local operators
title: U.S. Virgin Islands business licensing: who applies to DLCA?
description: Identify the local operator, site and services for DLCA licensing; distinguish brand rights, professional credentials and initial versus renewal tax steps.

sections.heading: What does a USVI business licence answer?
paragraphs: The U.S. Virgin Islands Department of Licensing and Consumer Affairs, or DLCA, explains the public licensing process for the identified local business and its actual activity. Your private brand agreement is a different permission: it cannot establish that the partner has completed DLCA, premises or applicable professional reviews.

Begin with three facts: which legal business will operate, on which island and at which site, and what work it will perform. Use those facts to organise the applicable reviews. The initial tax-clearance instruction and the qualified renewal treatment are different; neither can be substituted for the other.

sections.heading: Two permissions that answer different questions
paragraphs: Imagine that your company licenses its facilities-services brand to a partner on St. Thomas. The brand agreement answers questions such as which name and manuals the partner may use, what support you provide and what fees it pays. A government business licence answers a different question: may the identified local business carry on the relevant activity through the applicable public licensing process?

Write down the legal name of the business applying, any trading name, the proposed site on St. Thomas, St. Croix or St. John, and the actual services. This identifies whose application is being discussed. It also prevents your overseas company, a local subsidiary and an independent partner from being treated as the same applicant.

sections.heading: How to organise the application
paragraphs: DLCA’s instructions identify entity or trading-name registration, initial tax clearance, police review, zoning and applicable fire, health and professional-board review. These are different checks of the business, people, premises or activity. Some are handled electronically on the applicant’s behalf; the list does not mean the applicant must independently visit every agency in a fixed universal order.

First, assemble the entity and trading-name records. Next, describe the proposed services accurately enough for DLCA to identify the appropriate licence category. Then establish which location and activity reviews apply, who coordinates them and which records remain outstanding. Finally, retain the issued licence and required supporting approvals. Submitting an application proves that an application was made; it does not prove that the reviews have been completed.

sections.heading: Initial tax clearance and renewal are different
paragraphs: DLCA lists tax clearance in the initial application process. Its renewal instruction says that renewal applicants receive a licence without confirmation of tax clearance, while remaining responsible for current tax obligations and possible later action. Read that distinction carefully: renewal treatment does not remove the initial application step, and receiving a renewal does not mean unpaid tax obligations disappear.

The finance lead should therefore ask whether this is an initial application or a renewal, retain the relevant current instructions and record the tax task separately. Some links on the reviewed DLCA page are old, so confirm the current filing destination rather than assuming every linked office page still works.

sections.heading: Worked example: cleaning plus HVAC maintenance
paragraphs: Fictional example. A European facilities brand wants its island partner to sell cleaning and maintain air-conditioning equipment. HVAC means heating, ventilation and air conditioning. The partner assumes its private brand licence and one ordinary business application cover both services.

That assumption skips two questions. Cleaning and mechanical maintenance are different activities, and DLCA lists mechanical/HVAC professions among its board-certification categories. The technical lead must identify what the technicians will actually do and check the applicable board and personnel requirements. The brand’s training may explain its preferred method, but it does not establish a government qualification.

The premises lead separately checks the proposed site’s zoning and whichever fire or health reviews apply. A health inspection should not be added automatically to every cleaning business merely because it appears in a general list. If the mechanical-work answer is still missing, keep that part of the proposed service unresolved instead of describing the whole package as approved.

sections.heading: Try the decision: which part of the cleaning and HVAC plan is supported?
paragraphs: Continue the fictional example above. The partner has signed the brand agreement and submitted an ordinary business application. It has not yet established the relevant mechanical-work credentials or which site reviews apply. Before reading the answers, decide whether either document proves that the entire service bundle may start.

Answer: neither does. The signed agreement establishes private brand rights within its terms, and submission establishes that an application was made. The completed practice rows show what remains to investigate; they are management notes, not an additional legal form or a finding that every listed review applies.

sections.heading: Keep the remaining decisions separate
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule expressly includes a franchise located in a U.S. territory, subject to the applicable exemptions. Whether the relationship is a franchise and which disclosure duties apply must be checked separately from the operating licence. Independent territorial franchise or dealer relationship law remains unresolved in this guide.

The U.S. Virgin Islands are also outside the U.S. customs territory defined in the cited federal regulation. A plan to ship products or equipment therefore needs its own route-specific import review. A DLCA licence does not answer that shipment question.

sections.heading: The file your team should produce
paragraphs: Create a short application checklist naming the local operator, island, address, activities and licence category. For each required review, record the responsible person, application or approval document, current status and next question. Keep brand rights, government operating permission, professional credentials, tax and imports in separate rows. This is an optional way to organise the evidence; the actual required approvals depend on the activity and location.
The table assigns suggested responsibilities, rather than prescribing a staffing structure. The company secretary handles company records, and the CFO is the finance lead.

seoTitle: Guam foreign-company authority and service-business licences
title: Guam: separate foreign-company authority from service-business licensing
description: Identify the company conducting Guam business, the actual service category and separate worker questions before treating the partner’s licence as complete.

sections.heading: First identify the company doing the work
paragraphs: Suppose your Singapore parent signs a brand agreement, a local company contracts with Guam customers and a technical manager visits from overseas. The companies are connected commercially, but that does not make all their activities one company’s activities. List each entity, its contracts, premises, staff and services.

Under the cited corporate provision, a foreign corporation must obtain both a business licence and a certificate of authority before transacting business in Guam. The same section lists activities that, by themselves, are not transacting business. Owning a subsidiary alone is not automatically the parent conducting the subsidiary’s business. Apply the actual activity and entity-form provisions before deciding who must file.

sections.heading: Then classify the service
paragraphs: Guam’s general licensing chapter and its service-licensing chapter answer a different question from corporate authority. Chapter 76 describes an annual licence for covered non-professional service activity. Its description excludes services an employee provides to the employer, and section 76103 separately addresses services licensed under other provisions.

This matters when an ordinary service package includes regulated work. A maintenance business might clean equipment, repair electrical systems and provide engineering advice. It should not assume all three belong to the general-service category. Identify the actual tasks and any separate profession or trade route. An agency directory is a way to find the responsible office, not proof that every listed permit applies.

sections.heading: Worked example: the commissioning visit
paragraphs: Fictional example. A Singapore maintenance brand trains a Guam partner and sends a technical manager to help put customer equipment into operation. The local company will hire technicians, store parts and repair systems. The parent initially writes “Guam licensing handled by partner” in its plan.

The operating lead replaces that single statement with separate questions. What business is the parent itself conducting? What licences cover the partner’s actual services and premises? Does the visiting manager perform a regulated task? A general-service licence does not answer an electrical or engineering qualification question. Nor does a company filing answer whether a particular person may work. Until those answers are supported, the commissioning date is a proposal rather than a confirmed delivery promise.

sections.heading: Try the decision: whose activity does the document cover?
paragraphs: Use the fictional commissioning visit above. The parent signs the brand agreement, the local operator hires technicians and repairs systems, and a technical manager visits. Ask what evidence would justify replacing “the partner handles licensing” with a supported answer for each actor.

Answer: start with the parent’s own contracts, visits and services, not merely its ownership of the local company. The cited corporate provision requires the covered foreign corporation to obtain both a business licence and a certificate of authority before transacting business, but lists activities that by themselves do not constitute transacting. Owning a subsidiary alone does not decide that the parent conducts its business.

For the local operator, describe each service and identify the applicable general-service or separately licensed route. Chapter 76’s covered non-professional service description excludes employee-to-employer services, and section 76103 addresses services licensed elsewhere. For the visiting manager, the actual regulated task and permission to work remain separate questions. A correct company document cannot fill an unanswered person or professional-permission field.

sections.heading: Keep the company, job and shipment files separate
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule expressly includes franchises located in U.S. territories, subject to its exemptions. That does not decide independent Guam sales, relationship, tax or operating requirements. If the commercial arrangement needs franchise analysis, the business licence is a separate record.

Guam is outside the U.S. customs territory defined in the cited federal regulation. Identify the importing party, goods and actual route before copying mainland duty or quarantine assumptions. The employment and immigration questions also remain separate. Unknown charges or approval dates should stay unknown in the budget.

sections.heading: Prepare an entity-and-activity table
paragraphs: Use one row for each company and each distinct activity. Record the responsible agency, question, required evidence, task owner and status. The company secretary handles entity authority; operations describes services and premises; the technical lead identifies qualifications; and the people and supply leads handle workers and shipments. This table is an organising method, not a new legal filing requirement.

seoTitle: CNMI business licences: activity, location and nontransferability
title: Northern Mariana Islands: plan licences by business line and location
description: Use the CNMI activity-and-location rule, keep licences separate from company records and staffing, and do not assume an asset purchase transfers permission.

sections.heading: What the business-licence rule requires
paragraphs: The cited Commonwealth statute requires a licence before engaging in or continuing business. It calls for one general business licence for each business line at each Commonwealth location. Licences last one year and are nontransferable. Fees are set by regulation, so this guide does not supply a fee or treat an unverified amount as zero.

The same section also deals with temporary-event licences and other licensing categories. Ask Finance which category fits the facts instead of assuming the general description covers every activity. Separately, the Registrar’s document list covers domestic and foreign company registration, including foreign-company authority and good-standing records. A company-registration document does not replace the business licence.

sections.heading: Worked example: two islands and a new rental service
paragraphs: Fictional example. A facilities partner plans an office on Saipan, another on Tinian and a new equipment-rental activity. Its manager assumes one company means one licence. The actual rule requires the team to investigate both activities and places.

The operating lead creates a list of cleaning, maintenance and rental activities against each proposed location, then asks Finance to confirm the licence set. Customer sites are recorded separately so the authority can explain whether the operating pattern creates additional business-location questions. The partner’s commercial territory map does not decide that administrative classification. If it buys an existing operator’s equipment, it also checks its own licensing: buying assets does not transfer a nontransferable licence.

sections.heading: Try the decision: one company, which activities and places?
paragraphs: Continue the fictional Saipan/Tinian example. The partner lists cleaning, maintenance and rental at each proposed office. Before asking Finance for the licence set, decide whether “one company,” a sales-territory map or the list of actual activities and locations supplies the useful starting evidence.

Answer: use the activity-and-location list. The cited rule calls for one general business licence for each business line at each Commonwealth location, before engaging in or continuing business. The grid below is a completed preparation exercise, not a count of licences: Finance still needs to classify the activities and locations, including the distinct customer-site pattern.

Keep the one-year duration and nontransferability beside the licensing enquiry. A company registration is another record, and buying an existing operator’s equipment does not transfer its nontransferable licence. Unknown fees remain unknown; the grid does not make them zero.

sections.heading: A business licence does not supply the workforce
paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Labor describes a CW-1 route with employer conditions, prevailing-wage, recruitment and temporary labour-certification steps. A prevailing-wage determination is the programme’s wage decision for the actual job and worksite. Approved labour certification must come before the separate petition to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Certification alone does not authorise employment.

First test whether the plan can recruit and pay its local management team. If an overseas technician is essential, identify that person’s actual job and lawful route before promising a customer start date. CW-1 is not a promise of a place under a numerical limit or permission to move the worker to Guam or the mainland.

sections.heading: Check the other legal boundaries
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule includes franchises located in U.S. territories, subject to its exemptions. Independent territorial sales, dealer, relationship, advertising and sector requirements are not established as absent by this guide. They remain questions to investigate.

CNMI is outside the defined U.S. customs territory. Goods, quarantine and the receiving party need separate route-specific instructions. Do not use a mainland import spreadsheet as the legal answer for the islands.

sections.heading: What the management team should produce
paragraphs: Make a line-by-location licence list, with company records alongside it and renewal dates based on the issued licences. Add a staffing schedule showing employer, duties, worksite, wage evidence, recruitment, approvals and proposed start. Assign missing fees and dates to a person for investigation. These planning documents help prevent one uncompleted task from being hidden inside a confident opening date.

seoTitle: American Samoa: company permits and operating approvals
title: American Samoa: separate company permission, business licensing and people
description: Identify the trading entity, ownership-linked review and annual business-licence tasks; keep the visiting trainer’s approval on a separate track.

sections.heading: Begin with the entity that will trade
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s checklist describes a foreign-corporation permit application using certified company documents, corporate authorisation and resident-agent information. It separately directs the business to obtain business licensing before transacting business. The checklist identifies domestic and nonprofit corporations as exceptions to that named foreign-corporation law; the correct rules still depend on the actual entity type.

Write down which company will sign customers, employ the staff and receive the local revenue. An overseas brand owner and an independent operator are not automatically the same applicant. Then identify whether a parent company, local subsidiary or partner has the particular filing task.

sections.heading: Ownership can affect the review route
paragraphs: The official 2024 administrative compilation describes Territorial Planning Commission review linked to the applicant and ownership structure, and a separate immigration-board policy for business-licence applications submitted by people classified as aliens under the applicable rules. This guide does not decide any person’s American Samoan, residency or other legal status.

Prepare the ownership and control facts and ask the relevant agencies which route applies to this applicant. The compilation must be read with statutory definitions and any later changes. Avoid choosing an ownership label merely because it seems to make the form easier.

sections.heading: Worked example: a founder stays abroad but a trainer travels
paragraphs: Fictional example. An Asian facilities brand appoints a partner to run local contracts while its founder stays at home. The local partner says the brand agreement is signed, so it is ready to launch. The operations team discovers that an overseas supervisor must spend several weeks training crews at customer sites.

There are now several separate decisions. The company secretary identifies the operating entity’s permit and licence route. The local lead checks ownership-linked review. The people lead describes the supervisor’s actual tasks, dates and sponsor or employer. Calling the trip training does not establish permission to perform the work. The team keeps the customer launch date conditional while the necessary person-specific approval remains unresolved.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does the signed brand agreement complete the launch?
paragraphs: Use the fictional founder-abroad and visiting-trainer example. The local partner has signed the agreement. Ask which evidence belongs to the company, which belongs to ownership review, and which belongs to the individual who will train crews at customer sites.

Answer: the agreement establishes the agreed private rights, not completion of the public processes. The company file needs the actual trading entity and applicable foreign-corporation/business-licence route. The ownership file needs the facts relevant to the 2024 compilation’s described review, read with statutory definitions and later changes; this guide does not classify anyone’s legal status. The trainer file needs the person’s actual tasks, dates and employer or sponsor for the separate territorial enquiry.

Put business-licence renewal on the company calendar: the reviewed Commerce page identifies calendar-year expiry and October 1–December 31 renewal, with distinct late-fee and suspension treatment described above. Those dates cannot be copied into the trainer’s approval record. Use the companion people guide for that enquiry and retain the customer launch as conditional while a necessary answer is missing.

sections.heading: Entry approval is not a mainland visa assumption
paragraphs: American Samoa Legal Affairs explains that its entry rules differ from those of the United States and gives separate visitor and residency routes. Its residency instructions describe employment- and family-based petitions and say they must be approved before entry. A mainland U.S. visa, an ESTA travel assumption or a company business licence does not supply that territorial approval.
Record a non-sensitive summary of the person’s work, duration, employer or sponsor and approval status. Keep passports and actual immigration files in the authorised process outside this site.

sections.heading: Renewal and the other launch tasks
paragraphs: Commerce says business licences expire at calendar-year end and identifies October 1–December 31 for renewal. Its page separately explains post-January 1 late-fee and January 31 suspension treatment. Retain the issued licence and confirm current instructions; do not merge this annual calendar with a worker’s approval dates.

The federal Franchise Rule includes a franchise located in a U.S. territory, subject to its exemptions. Independent local sales and relationship-law questions remain open. American Samoa is outside the U.S. customs territory, so local imports, quarantine and the exact premises also need their own checks.

sections.heading: Build one approval map with separate rows
paragraphs: List the company-permit decision, operating licence and ownership review, each necessary person’s route, and the actual premises and imports. For each, record the responsible person, evidence, missing question and the commitment that depends on it. The map is an optional management aid; it does not convert an incomplete application into an approval.

rows: Issued license and required agency decisions

seoTitle: U.S. territory customs boundaries: Puerto Rico, Guam and more
title: Shipping to U.S. territories: which side of the customs boundary?
description: Compare the defined customs boundary for five territories; separate that finding from product entry, duties, territorial taxes and onward-shipment treatment.

sections.heading: What the cited definition establishes
paragraphs: The federal regulation defines the U.S. customs territory as the states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa and the U.S. Virgin Islands are outside that defined area. Each therefore needs its own destination-and-route investigation.

This is a boundary finding, not a calculation. It supplies neither a duty rate nor permission for a product to enter. It also does not decide the treatment of a later shipment from a territory to the mainland. Those are additional questions about the actual goods and route.

sections.heading: Use the comparison to ask the right next question
paragraphs: Read each row as a starting point for research. “Inside” does not mean every shipment is tax-free, and “outside” does not supply a particular tariff. Local taxes, product controls and the identity of the responsible importer still need evidence.

sections.heading: Worked example: the same replacement machine, two destinations
paragraphs: Fictional example. A Dutch service brand plans to send replacement equipment to partners in Puerto Rico and Guam. The finance team copies the Puerto Rico spreadsheet and changes only the shipping address for Guam. This preserves the appearance of a complete quote while leaving the legal route untested.

The supply lead instead records each receiving company, port, product specification, origin and intended use. It asks which official customs and quarantine instructions apply to each journey and who will make the entry. Until the classification and applicable charges are supported, the duty cells remain unknown. A freight quote can still be recorded, but it should not be presented as the complete landed cost.

sections.heading: Try the shipment: what changes when the destination changes?
paragraphs: In the fictional Dutch equipment example, the team has a Puerto Rico cost sheet and wants to use it for Guam. Before reading the answer, decide whether changing the destination preserves the customs-boundary assumption and whether either classification supplies a duty rate.

Answer: Puerto Rico is inside the cited definition of U.S. customs territory; Guam is outside it. That difference requires a route-specific investigation, not a guessed tariff. The five destination answers below are boundary findings only: “inside” is not tax-free treatment, and “outside” supplies neither a duty amount nor unrestricted entry.

For each shipment, the supply lead still needs the receiving party, product, origin, destination port, intended use, importer and any onward route. Keep the freight quote and commercial costs separate from legal charges. An unknown duty cell stays unknown until supported; a contingency does not answer the legal question.

sections.heading: Keep legal charges separate from planning allowances
paragraphs: A carrier price, broker fee and storage estimate are commercial costs. A duty or tax is a legal charge that needs the relevant authority and facts. A contingency is money you choose to hold for uncertainty. Do not combine them into one unexplained percentage or use the contingency as evidence that an unknown legal charge has been resolved.

sections.heading: Build one factsheet for each shipment route
paragraphs: Include the product and intended use, manufacturer and origin evidence, proposed classification, exporting party, importer, receiving entity, destination port and any onward shipment. Add the official source and date for each legal charge, and the quote and date for commercial costs. Assign each unanswered question before approving an order. This is a practical costing method; it does not itself authorise a shipment.

seoTitle: CNMI CW-1 staffing: labour certification versus work permission
title: CNMI CW-1 staffing: what must happen before a worker can start?
description: Separate the actual employer, wage and recruitment steps, DOL certification and the later USCIS petition before promising a worker start date.

sections.heading: Identify the employer and the real job first
paragraphs: DOL describes participation conditions including a physical CNMI business location, an employer relationship and a Federal Employer Identification Number, the federal identifying number used by the employer. The job, worksite and actual hiring entity matter. An overseas brand’s need for technical support does not by itself establish that the employer, role or individual fits this route.

Write a job description with the actual duties, supervisor, location, proposed wage and needed start date. Do this separately for a locally recruited manager and an overseas specialist; their situations are not interchangeable.

sections.heading: Keep the stages in the right relationship
paragraphs: The DOL page describes prevailing-wage, required U.S.-worker recruitment and temporary labour-certification steps. The employer needs approved temporary labour certification before the separate USCIS petition. Completing the labour application alone does not establish that the person may start work.

Ask for the current requirements and evidence at each stage, including the separate approval and status needed for employment. This guide does not choose an occupation code, predict availability under a numerical limit or decide anyone’s eligibility.

sections.heading: Worked example: a pilot needing a commissioning technician
paragraphs: Fictional example. A technical-services brand expects to hire a local manager but needs an overseas technician to put customer equipment into service. The sales team promises a fixed launch date because the specialist has agreed to travel.

Agreement to travel is not the missing legal evidence. The people lead first identifies the actual employer, job and worksite, then maps recruitment, wage and certification requirements and the separate immigration stage. The COO checks whether a supported start date fits the customer contract. If the lawful route is unresolved, the business may change the delivery plan, recruit differently or pause the commitment. It should not turn the intended date into an approved date.

sections.heading: Try the timeline: what has—and has not—been completed?
paragraphs: Use the fictional pilot needing local management and an overseas commissioning technician. Ask whether customer demand, a target opening date or completed recruitment can establish that the technician may begin. Then identify the evidence needed for the actual employer and job.

Answer: those commercial or preparatory events do not supply work permission. The reviewed route connects employer/job facts, prevailing-wage and recruitment steps to approved temporary labour certification before the separate USCIS petition. Certification alone does not authorise employment. Keep the local manager’s hiring plan and the overseas technician’s route as separate records rather than treating “staffing ready” as one event.

If an essential stage remains unsupported, the operations lead must reconsider the promised scope or date instead of recording the desired start as approved.

seoTitle: American Samoa visiting trainers: entry and work questions
title: American Samoa visiting trainers: check activities before arranging travel
description: Describe a trainer’s actual work, dates and sponsor before selecting the territorial entry or residence route; company licensing is a separate task.

sections.heading: The territorial instructions are the starting point
paragraphs: American Samoa Legal Affairs says that its entry rules differ from those of the United States and gives separate visitor and residency routes. Its residency page describes employment- and family-based petitions and says they must be completed and approved before entry. The applicable route still depends on the individual and the intended activities.

A mainland visa, a franchise agreement or the corporation’s business licence does not answer those person-specific questions. Keep the proposed visit, residence and physical work separate when describing the facts.

sections.heading: Worked example: four weeks described as training
paragraphs: Fictional example. A European facilities brand schedules four weeks of training in American Samoa. The visiting supervisor will show local staff procedures, direct crews during live contracts and resolve customer problems. The team assumes the trip is routine because it is short and the visitor remains employed overseas.

The people lead replaces the broad label with a daily activity description. It records the work locations, duration, local sponsor or employer, reporting line and customer-facing duties. Those facts allow the responsible process to be checked. This article does not classify the trip as permitted or prohibited; it shows why its name alone is insufficient. If approval is not supported, operations needs an alternative delivery plan rather than an unsupported promise that the trainer will arrive.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does “four weeks of training” answer the question?
paragraphs: Use the fictional trainer above, who will also direct live crews and troubleshoot customer work. Ask whether the short itinerary, overseas employment or the word training determines the applicable territorial route.

Answer: none of those descriptions alone supplies the permission. The people lead needs a non-sensitive account of the actual duties, dates, relevant status facts and employer or sponsor, then the applicable territorial instructions. American Samoa’s entry arrangements are distinct from mainland U.S. assumptions, and the reviewed residency instructions say the employment- and family-based petitions described there must be approved before entry.

The useful output is a specific unanswered question with a responsible person, not an invented visa category or a conclusion that the trainer may work. Keep the business’s annual licence renewal on a different calendar and private identity/immigration documents in the authorised process outside this site.

sections.heading: Write a useful brief without collecting private files
paragraphs: Record nationality and current status only as factual inputs to be checked through the authorised process. Add the exact proposed duties, dates, employer or sponsor and a short note of what is approved or still pending. Identify the relevant agency or adviser and who will obtain the answer.

The actual passport, immigration application and sensitive supporting records belong in the authorised private process. The planning brief needs a reference and responsible person, not copies of those documents.

sections.heading: Keep the business’s annual calendar separate
paragraphs: Commerce’s business-licence page states calendar-year expiry and an October 1–December 31 renewal period, with separately described late-fee and suspension treatment. The operating entity needs that calendar even when a visiting worker’s timing changes.

A renewed business licence is evidence about the business’s licensing process, not proof of the supervisor’s immigration status. Conversely, a person’s approval does not renew the company’s licence. Put the two records on separate lines and identify who maintains each.

sections.heading: What to decide before booking
paragraphs: Confirm which route is being investigated, what approval must precede entry and what evidence will support the proposed work. Link any unresolved person-specific step to the training or customer-start date. If the essential person cannot start in time, decide whether another supported staffing arrangement, a different service scope or a later launch is workable.

seoTitle: Pittsburgh registration for outside service businesses
title: Pittsburgh business registration: outside offices and city customer work
description: Check the actual city service and commencement facts, the published 15-day provision and Finance verification before calling registration complete.

sections.heading: Why the customer location matters
paragraphs: The city’s official registration page includes a business located outside Pittsburgh that performs work or services in whole or in part within the city. The operating lead therefore needs the actual customer sites and activities, not only the company’s registered office.

The page quotes a 15-day registration provision. Match that provision to the actual commencement facts before fixing the business’s due date. A missing start date should prompt a question, not a guessed date or an assumption that no registration is needed.

sections.heading: The form and the confirmation are different records
paragraphs: The same page says registration is not complete until Finance issues verification. Keep the submitted information and the issued confirmation separately so the team can see which stage has been reached. A payment receipt or account reference may help track an application, but it should not be relabelled as the verification itself.

This distinction matters when another team relies on the registration before making a commitment. The useful question is “What record confirms this stage is complete?” rather than “Has someone started the paperwork?”

sections.heading: Worked example: crews crossing the city boundary
paragraphs: Fictional example. A foreign cleaning brand’s partner rents an office outside Pittsburgh. It wins a contract to clean a customer’s premises inside the city and assumes its office municipality is the only place to investigate.

The COO records the local contracting entity, customer address, service and actual start date. Finance checks the city provision against those facts and follows the registration process if applicable. It then retains the verification when issued. If the application has only been submitted, the plan says so; it does not display “registered” merely because a form or payment was sent.

sections.heading: Try the decision: submitted or registered?
paragraphs: In the fictional cleaning example, the partner’s office is outside Pittsburgh and its customer’s premises are inside. Before reading the answer, identify the relevant activity and commencement facts, then decide what an application confirmation would prove.

Answer: the official page includes an outside business performing work or services wholly or partly in Pittsburgh, so the customer-site work belongs in the enquiry. Match the quoted 15-day provision to the actual commencement facts rather than inventing a deadline from the contract-signing or incorporation date. This exercise supplies no date calculation because those actual facts must first be established.

An application confirmation proves submission. The page says registration is not complete until Finance issues verification, so the team should keep a separate field for that issued record. Any premises, regulated-work or franchise-sales question remains separate even after the registration stage is complete.

sections.heading: What this registration does not decide
paragraphs: A registration record is different from permission to use a particular premises or carry on regulated professional work. If the business also opens a depot or performs a regulated activity, the premises or technical lead must investigate that separate question. The city registration also does not determine whether the overseas brand’s commercial arrangement is a franchise or whether its sales process meets disclosure rules.
Keep uncertain fees and additional requirements visible. This guide explains one published process; it is not evidence that every other obligation has been checked.

sections.heading: Make a city-work register
paragraphs: List the operating entity, each relevant Pittsburgh site, the service, commencement facts and person responsible for the registration decision. Attach references to the application and issued verification, then identify any separate premises or sector questions. This is a practical management record, not an additional filing created by this guide.

seoTitle: Atlanta occupation-tax certificate and zoning review
title: Atlanta: separate the occupation-tax certificate from zoning review
description: Distinguish ATLBIZ tax certification from Accela zoning and applicable permits; payment or submission does not prove an issued opening record.

sections.heading: Two applications can support one opening
paragraphs: The current ATL311 instruction separates the occupation-tax application in ATLBIZ from a location zoning review through Accela. It also identifies applicable regulatory permits. These steps answer different questions: identifying the business for the tax process does not establish that the location is suitable for its proposed use.

Use the legal entity, actual activity and address consistently. A general description such as “services” may hide storage, equipment or customer visits that the premises team needs to describe. Ask which reviews apply to the real proposal rather than treating the agency’s whole directory as a universal permit list.

sections.heading: Issuance comes after the required material
paragraphs: The instructions describe issuance following required documents and payment. An account, submitted application or application charge is therefore not the certificate. Record what has been submitted, what other review is outstanding and what issued document will show completion.

A processing estimate can help organise the schedule, but it is not a guaranteed opening date. The business should link any customer or premises commitment to the actual approvals that commitment depends on.

sections.heading: Worked example: the portal looks complete
paragraphs: Fictional example. A partner sets up ATLBIZ and pays an application charge. Its manager tells the overseas brand that Atlanta licensing is finished. The proposed unit’s zoning approval has not yet been obtained.

The launch lead asks for the issued certificate and discovers the missing location task. The premises lead takes responsibility for the zoning review and the evidence needed in the application process. The team records the tax application as submitted and the overall certificate as pending. It does not assume paying again or opening another account would resolve the zoning question.

sections.heading: Try the decision: why is the paid application still incomplete?
paragraphs: Use the fictional portal example above. Finance can show a payment and a submitted tax application, but zoning review is unfinished. Ask which document establishes the tax-application stage and which evidence is missing for the proposed site.

Answer: Atlanta’s occupation-tax process and the location review are different tasks, using the ATLBIZ and Accela processes described above. Required documents and payment precede issuance; a payment is not the issued certificate. Unfinished zoning cannot be marked complete merely because a related tax screen looks complete.

The project lead should return separate evidence for the tax application/certificate, zoning outcome and any activity-specific permit that actually applies. That is not a universal list or fixed sequence for every Atlanta business, and no submitted date is a guaranteed opening or processing date.

sections.heading: Organise the documents by the question they answer
paragraphs: Keep entity and trading-name information together, location/use evidence together, and the occupation-tax application, payment and issued certificate together. Add a separate row for any activity-specific permit. This lets the business see whether the problem is identity, premises, missing documents, payment or a separate regulated activity.
Other tax, employment, sector and franchise-sales questions remain independent. This guide’s narrow city process does not classify the brand agreement or supply all permissions for the work.

sections.heading: A useful next request
paragraphs: Give the local lead a one-page list of the entity, address and proposed uses. Ask them to identify the ATLBIZ stage, the Accela review and any applicable permit, with the responsible person and evidence for each. The result should show precisely what is issued and what remains outstanding, rather than a single ambiguous “licence done” checkbox.

seoTitle: City of Miami: Certificate of Use and business-tax receipts
title: City of Miami: check the use certificate and city/county tax receipts
description: Identify the City of Miami boundary, the qualified use-certificate step and separate city and Miami-Dade County receipts for the actual site and activity.

sections.heading: Find the correct local government first
paragraphs: Record the exact premises and whether they are inside City of Miami boundaries. The customer’s mailing label or a commercial description of the area does not settle that question. Also identify the actual company conducting the business, because the overseas brand owner and the local operator may be different entities.
Once the authority is known, use its process for the actual activity. A county instruction for an unincorporated area should not simply be copied onto a City of Miami unit.

sections.heading: The city generally puts use before the tax receipt
paragraphs: The city’s published process generally sequences a Certificate of Use before its Business Tax Receipt, while stating exceptions. Check whether the use requirement or an exception fits the actual proposal; do not assume every business follows an identical route.

The city also directs businesses to a separate Miami-Dade County local business tax receipt. Keep city and county records distinct. Obtaining one does not demonstrate that the other was obtained or that a premises review has been completed.

sections.heading: Worked example: a depot serving customers across the county
paragraphs: Fictional example. A service operator stores equipment in a City of Miami unit and sends teams to customers throughout Miami-Dade. The manager receives county guidance and assumes it describes every approval for the depot.

The premises lead first confirms the unit’s municipality and asks how the proposed storage and operating use fit the city’s use-certificate process. Finance records the city tax receipt and county tax receipt as separate tasks. The wider customer service area is also recorded for any additional questions, but it does not change the depot’s municipality. If an exception is claimed, the file records its actual basis instead of leaving the use-certificate box blank.

sections.heading: Try the decision: which Miami authority and which record?
paragraphs: Use the fictional depot serving county-wide customers. The actual depot is inside the City of Miami, but the manager has relied on a county guide. Ask whether its service territory or postal market label selects the local premises process.

Answer: start with the exact address and responsible local government. The City of Miami generally places its Certificate of Use before the city Business Tax Receipt, with stated exceptions; the Miami-Dade County receipt is separate. A site in unincorporated county territory calls for its own applicable route rather than automatic use of the city process.

For the city depot, record three distinct questions: the use certificate or applicable exception, the city receipt and the county receipt. Retain each actual issued record or supported exception. This is not a finding that those records complete fire, health, professional or every other opening requirement.

sections.heading: Keep site, tax and professional evidence separate
paragraphs: A use certificate, local tax receipt and professional credential serve different purposes. Describe the services accurately so any separate trade, health, fire or other activity question can be assigned to the appropriate person. This article does not supply those answers for an unidentified activity.

The same separation applies to the brand relationship. Government operating documents do not prove compliance with franchise-sales rules, and a private brand licence does not replace government records. Unknown fees or additional requirements remain questions to investigate.

sections.heading: The document to request from your local lead
paragraphs: Ask for an address-and-entity checklist with three initial rows: the city use-certificate decision, city Business Tax Receipt and county receipt. For each, record applicability, current application or issued document, responsible person and next action. Then add any separately identified activity permissions. This is an optional way to manage the process, not a declaration that the list is complete for every business.

seoTitle: Jacksonville Local Business Tax Receipt versus occupancy
title: Jacksonville: distinguish the business-tax receipt and occupancy decision
description: Keep the Local Business Tax Receipt, commercial occupancy question and any separate municipal route distinct for the actual address and proposed activity.

sections.heading: Two questions can remain open at different times
paragraphs: The local tax receipt concerns covered business activity. The Certificate of Use concerns the new or expanding commercial operation’s use process. The city’s tax page separates them, so recording one should not automatically close the other.

The cited rule calls for the local tax receipt before covered business, while the use certificate and any other approvals have their own applicable requirements. The team should identify those requirements for the actual activity and site, rather than infer a universal sequence from whichever document arrives first.

sections.heading: Check the municipality, not just the market name
paragraphs: The official instructions also identify additional municipal tax routes for the beach municipalities and Baldwin. A business describing its market as Jacksonville should still record the precise location of each operation. A second site may need a different local enquiry from the first.

This is particularly relevant to a service brand with one depot and customers across the wider area. Record the depot and customer work separately so the responsible authority can answer the question for the real operating pattern.

sections.heading: Worked example: finance has a receipt, operations has a gap
paragraphs: Fictional example. A new commercial depot receives its local tax receipt. Finance marks that document as received and tells the overseas brand that the opening paperwork is finished. The use certificate is still unresolved.

The receipt is genuine evidence, but it answers only its own question. The launch lead keeps the premises-use task open and asks the premises lead for the required determination and document. A proposed second operation in Jacksonville Beach is put on a separate line for that municipality’s local-tax question. The team now has two clear outstanding decisions rather than one misleading green opening indicator.

sections.heading: Try the decision: can finance release both sites?
paragraphs: Use the fictional depot and Jacksonville Beach site above. Finance has a local tax receipt, but the depot’s occupancy question is unresolved. Ask whether that receipt also answers the new or expanding commercial-space enquiry or the second municipality’s route.

Answer: it answers only the process to which the receipt belongs. The Local Business Tax Receipt and the Certificate of Occupancy question are different, and the reviewed guidance identifies a separate occupancy enquiry for new or expanding commercial premises. The actual municipality also matters: the beaches municipalities and Baldwin have additional routes to investigate.

Keep one address row for the depot and another for the Jacksonville Beach proposal. In each, record the tax receipt, the actual use/occupancy question, applicable authority and missing evidence. Do not impose one universal sequence or label an unanswered second-site enquiry “not required.”

sections.heading: What to retain and who should answer
paragraphs: Keep the entity, actual activities, addresses and proposed start dates with the relevant applications and issued documents. Finance owns the tax-record evidence. The premises lead owns the use enquiry. A technical lead checks any separate regulated service. Their tasks may depend on one another, but one person’s completed record does not prove the whole operation is authorised.

sections.heading: A narrow process, not a complete permission list
paragraphs: Ask the local lead for a table showing the tax receipt, use certificate and applicable additional municipal questions, with an owner and evidence for each. Fees, sector requirements and unrelated obligations remain unknown where not checked. Neither a tax receipt nor a use record determines whether the brand’s agreement is a franchise or satisfies its sales-disclosure duties.

seoTitle: Kansas City, Missouri: zoning, business and trade licences
title: Kansas City, Missouri: separate zoning, city licensing and trade work
description: Describe the actual office, workshop and trade tasks for Kansas City, Missouri; keep state-law licensing exemptions and separate sector requirements visible.

sections.heading: Confirm which city is responsible
paragraphs: Start with the actual premises and municipality. A commercial sales territory does not identify the government office responsible for the site. An address in Kansas requires a different jurisdictional investigation from an address covered by this Missouri guide.

Also identify the operating entity and describe what happens at the site: office administration, storage, workshop activity, customer visits or actual trade work. These facts make the enquiry usable for the authority rather than leaving it at the broad label “industrial services.”

sections.heading: What the BizCare guide separates
paragraphs: The official guide identifies zoning clearance for new businesses with a KCMO address and address changes, city registration or licensing, and additional industry requirements. A location decision, a business record and a permission for regulated work answer different questions.

The general guidance acknowledges state-law exemptions. Check whether an actual exemption fits the activity instead of treating it as permission for all businesses. Resolve the applicable prerequisites before licence issuance and operation; a completed online account is not a substitute for that evidence.

sections.heading: Worked example: the workshop and the construction task
paragraphs: Fictional example. An industrial-services partner rents a workshop at a KCMO address and intends to perform a regulated construction trade. It initially asks only for the city business licence.

The premises lead investigates whether the proposed workshop use has the necessary zoning clearance. Finance or the local operating lead handles the city business record. The technical lead separately checks the permission for the construction work. A licence in one column is not evidence in the others. If the business later moves, the published address-change point prompts another location enquiry rather than simply editing its stationery.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does “service company” describe enough?
paragraphs: Use the fictional industrial-services workshop above. Compare an office-only description with the actual storage, workshop activity and construction-related task. Ask which facts the BizCare/location enquiry needs and which belong to a trade-permission enquiry.

Answer: the broad service-company name is insufficient. For the Kansas City, Missouri site, describe the address, storage, equipment, customer access and actual work so the relevant location/zoning and city-licence routes can be identified. Keep the stated state-law exemptions in that licensing branch; this guide does not say every service has one identical city-licence duty.

A regulated construction or professional task needs its own actual-task enquiry, not permission inferred from the workshop’s city record. The exercise selects facts to investigate, not a final trade classification. It concerns Kansas City, Missouri, and supplies no process for Kansas City, Kansas.

sections.heading: Make the question specific enough to answer
paragraphs: Give the authority a written description of the entity, premises and services. Ask which city category and any state-law exemption are being considered, what evidence is needed for the address and which office handles the regulated trade. Retain the answer with the relevant application or issued record.

Unknown fees remain unknown. The article does not supply every trade licence, tax or employment rule, or establish that an offer of franchise rights is permitted. Those questions stay separate from the narrow city opening process.

sections.heading: The useful management output
paragraphs: Prepare a three-part checklist: location clearance, city business record and activity-specific permission. Name an owner and the required evidence for each. This checklist is an optional way to coordinate the work; it should reveal missing answers rather than turn broad guidance into a claim that the premises can open.

seoTitle: Baltimore City business licences: clerk versus tax account
title: Baltimore City: distinguish the licence clerk, County and tax account
description: Match the actual Baltimore City location and activity to the correct clerk and licence category; a Maryland sales-tax account answers a separate question.

sections.heading: The state and the clerk answer different questions
paragraphs: Maryland’s Comptroller separates sales/use-tax registration from business-licence categories that may apply through the Clerk of Circuit Court. Those licences are issued in the county or Baltimore City where the business is located. The actual activity determines which category needs investigation; this guide does not say every service business needs every clerk licence.

A state tax account identifies a tax-registration step. It does not prove that the operator has obtained an applicable licence, that the premises have approved use or that a worker holds a professional qualification.

sections.heading: Why the address changes the enquiry
paragraphs: A contact sheet headed Baltimore County is not automatically appropriate for a Baltimore City premises. Confirm the legal jurisdiction from the actual address before choosing the clerk. Keep the proposed operating entity and trading name with that address so the records refer to the same business.

This matters when a brand serves the wider Baltimore market from several locations. Market coverage is a commercial description; the licence application still needs the relevant government area and activity.

sections.heading: Worked example: adding equipment sales to a service workshop
paragraphs: Fictional example. A service operator adds a workshop selling equipment in Baltimore City. Its accountant starts with a Baltimore County contact list and points to the existing sales-tax account as evidence that registration is finished.

The company secretary corrects the jurisdiction and describes the actual mix of goods and services to the City clerk’s process. The team asks which category applies and retains the resulting instructions or issued licence. Finance keeps the state tax account as separate evidence. The enquiry does not assume equipment sales and servicing receive identical treatment, or that the address can be ignored because the brand already operates elsewhere.

sections.heading: Try the decision: which office answers the added-sales question?
paragraphs: Use the fictional workshop that adds equipment sales. The accountant has a Maryland tax account and Baltimore County contact details. Ask whether those records establish the City licence category for the actual activity.

Answer: neither settles that category. Baltimore City is distinct from Baltimore County. The state Comptroller’s sales/use-tax account and the Clerk of the Circuit Court’s business-licensing role answer different questions. Here the clerk is being consulted about an administrative licensing process, not because the business has a lawsuit.

Prepare the City address, legal operator and separate service/sales activities for the correct enquiry. Whether a particular licence category applies depends on the activity; the exercise does not declare every service subject to the same licence or decide the workshop’s final category.

sections.heading: Prepare the records in a way another person can check
paragraphs: Create one row for the state tax account, one for the clerk category decision and any required issued licence, and one for premises or regulated-work questions identified separately. Include the exact entity, address, activity, authority and responsible person. Distinguish an application or payment from the actual issued record.

Use the current instructions for fees and timing. Nothing here establishes all local, trade, employment or franchise-sales requirements. If the category is uncertain, record the question and the person obtaining the answer rather than entering “not required” without support.

seoTitle: Houston commercial-space occupancy: proposed-use checks
title: Houston commercial occupancy: check the space’s proposed use
description: Check the City of Houston site, unit and proposed commercial use before relying on a prior occupancy record; detailed filing instructions remain unresolved.

sections.heading: First make sure this is a City of Houston site
paragraphs: The Houston metropolitan area is wider than the City of Houston, and Harris County is not the same jurisdiction as the city. Confirm the precise parcel, address and individual unit. A Houston mailing address or a broker’s market description is not enough to choose the permitting office.
Also identify the entity that will occupy the space. The relevant premises question concerns that operator’s proposed use, not merely the fact that an earlier tenant ran a business in the building.

sections.heading: What the city’s occupancy guidance says
paragraphs: The city business page says a certificate of occupancy is required before a commercial building or individual lease space is occupied, or when its occupancy classification changes. The tenant should therefore obtain the current record and compare it with what it proposes to do.

Describe storage, chemicals, powered equipment, public access, layout and proposed alterations as applicable. Houston’s page describes separate building, fire, food and other permitting and inspection activities. The correct combination depends on the actual site and operation; the list does not make every permit mandatory for every service business.

sections.heading: Worked example: a cleaning company’s service bay
paragraphs: Fictional example. A cleaning operator rents a bay described as commercial. It plans to store products, dispatch staff and keep powered equipment there. The landlord points to the building’s history and says another business already used the unit.

The local lead requests the current CO, exact unit identification and permitted use. It then gives the authority the proposed storage and layout rather than asking whether a cleaning brand is generally allowed. The question is whether the existing evidence fits this proposal and which further reviews apply. The article does not conclude that the bay fails or passes; it explains what information is missing.

sections.heading: Try the decision: what does the landlord’s prior-use statement prove?
paragraphs: Use the fictional cleaning-company service bay above. The landlord says the space was used commercially before. Ask whether that statement identifies the authorised use for this unit or shows that the proposed storage, chemicals, equipment and public access fit it.

Answer: it does neither by itself. The reviewed City of Houston summary says a CO is needed before commercial buildings or individual lease spaces are occupied and when the relevant occupancy classification changes. The operator must compare the actual unit and proposed use with the relevant record rather than treating “commercial” as the whole classification.

Request the prior record and put the actual proposed activities beside it. The next step is an address-and-use enquiry supported by those facts, not a fee estimate or filing sequence supplied here. The detailed city permitting PDFs were inaccessible, so current application steps, technical classification, fees and processing time remain unresolved. A labelled rent-delay scenario can help finance understand exposure; it is not the city’s timetable.

sections.heading: Link the lease schedule to actual answers
paragraphs: Record any difference between the lease address, unit number and official documents. Ask which inspections or approvals would be needed before the planned use. Then link those tasks to the dates when rent, equipment orders and customer promises create costs.

This is optional business planning, not a rule that every lease must contain a particular clause. Its purpose is to make the consequences visible: an unresolved occupancy question should not disappear merely because finance has entered an opening date.

sections.heading: What is still unknown
paragraphs: The detailed Houston Permitting Center PDFs were access-blocked during the underlying research. This page therefore supplies no full procedure, current fee, classification outcome or parcel approval. Building, fire, environmental and sector requirements remain to be confirmed for the actual operation.

Prepare an address-and-use file containing the current CO, layout, proposed activities, landlord documents, authority response, responsible person and missing approvals. It should show what is supported and what must be answered before the team relies on the premises.

seoTitle: NYC CO, temporary CO, LNO and Letter of Completion
title: New York City: distinguish the CO, TCO and building letters
description: Compare NYC occupancy documents by purpose and conditions; keep the pre-1938 qualification and CO-request system cutoff tied to the right question.

sections.heading: Start with the authorised use, not the advertising label
paragraphs: DOB describes a CO as establishing legal use or occupancy. A new building requires a CO, while relevant changes to use, occupancy or egress—the ways people leave the premises—can require a new or amended certificate. The actual change matters; this article does not classify your proposed activity.

Ask for the record matching the property and unit. A description such as commercial building does not show whether the proposed training, storage or other activity matches its legal use. A TCO also needs to be recognised as temporary rather than treated as a final certificate.

sections.heading: Why the building’s age does not answer everything
paragraphs: DOB explains that certain lawful buildings built before 1938 may not have a CO unless later changes have triggered the requirement. That is a conditional historical route, not an automatic exemption for every old property.

An LNO can confirm legal use under its stated conditions. A Letter of Completion concerns qualifying work that did not require a new or amended CO. These letters have different purposes. Neither should be treated as a universal replacement for the occupancy evidence needed for a new business proposal.

sections.heading: Find the relevant CO-request records
paragraphs: For CO requests before March 1, 2021, DOB directs users to BIS. For requests on or after that date, it directs them to DOB NOW. This is a cutoff for the CO-request search, not a statement that every kind of building record moved systems on that date.

Check the precise property and relevant systems, then compare the documents with the proposed activity and alterations. Record open applications, violations and required sign-offs as well as the certificate or letter. One document should not hide another unresolved part of the property record.

sections.heading: Worked example: an old office becomes a training location
paragraphs: Fictional example. A corporate-training operator considers a pre-1938 office building. The landlord provides a contractor’s completion letter for earlier work. The operator assumes the age and letter together settle permission for the planned classes.

The premises lead instead asks which document establishes the legal use, what the completion letter actually covers, and whether the proposed training activity and occupancy fit that evidence. The lead also identifies any required new or amended record. This reasoning does not produce a capacity figure or approval; it prevents the team from relying on the wrong document.

sections.heading: Try the documents: which question does each answer?
paragraphs: Use the fictional pre-1938 office proposed for training. The landlord offers a contractor’s completion letter. Before reading the answers, ask which evidence concerns legal use, which concerns completed work, and whether age alone establishes permission for the proposed classes.

Answer: those are different questions. The table below summarises the reviewed DOB distinctions; an actual contractor letter must first be identified rather than assumed to be a particular DOB document. Certain lawful pre-1938 buildings may have no CO unless later changes triggered the requirement, but age alone does not settle the new proposal.

For CO-request records, the reviewed cutoff is before March 1, 2021 for BIS and on or after that date for DOB NOW. That statement concerns the CO-request search, not all building records. Compare the actual documents, property/unit and proposed activity, retaining any open applications, violations and sign-off questions; this exercise supplies no capacity or approval.

sections.heading: Prepare a document-purpose table
paragraphs: List each CO, TCO or letter, its property/unit, date, purpose and any conditions. Put the proposed use and planned alterations beside it, then note what remains to be confirmed with DOB. Keep the lease, fire, accessibility, sector and other questions separate. The table is a planning aid, not a property clearance or a substitute for the actual records.

seoTitle: San Jose café takeover: Santa Clara County food permits
title: San Jose food takeover: distinguish the buyer’s permit and proposed changes
description: Identify Santa Clara County DEH’s new-operator and change-review questions before relying on the seller’s food permit or planning an opening.

sections.heading: Treat the buyer as a new operator
paragraphs: For a proposed fixed retail food site in San Jose, the county says an operating permit cannot pass to a new owner. A takeover requires a facility evaluation, and the new operator must obtain its own health permit before operating. The county offers evaluation before purchase, making it useful when deciding whether to acquire the business.

The seller’s trading history may help you investigate the premises, but it does not prove that your new company can begin operating under the seller’s permission. Identify the actual new operator and ownership-change date.

sections.heading: Describe the change before selecting the application route
paragraphs: The county’s October 2026 evaluation packet asks about the owner, dates, food preparation, menu, equipment and remodelling. Provide the menu where food preparation occurs. Changed menus, new equipment or major structural deficiencies can lead from evaluation to plan review.

The plan-review page lists information such as scope of work, equipment, finishes, mechanical/plumbing/electrical details, applicable hoods, menu and equipment specifications. A complete application and required payment precede the review queue. Approved plans are followed by appropriate construction inspections and separate operating-permit steps; entering a queue is not approval.

sections.heading: Worked example: a café adds cooked hot food
paragraphs: Fictional example. A foreign café brand buys a San Jose café and keeps its counter, but adds cooking equipment and a hot-food menu. The buyer initially budgets only a takeover evaluation because the address already has food use.

The operations lead compares the existing and proposed menu, food preparation, equipment and hood arrangements. It asks County DEH to confirm whether the changes require plan review rather than assuming an evaluation alone is sufficient. Finance then keeps evaluation, plans, construction and the operating permit as separate cost questions. Before a nonrefundable fit-out deposit, the premises lead also obtains the city’s actual building, use and fire answers. County food review does not supply those city decisions.

sections.heading: Try the takeover: what if the dining area looks unchanged?
paragraphs: Use the fictional café adding cooked hot food and equipment. Ask which two facts need separate attention: the identity of the buyer/operator and changes to the menu, process, equipment or structure. Does the appearance of an existing café answer either question?

Answer: the county food permit is nontransferable, so the buyer needs its own operating-permit answer before operating. Separately, the actual changes determine the relevant plan-review enquiry. An unchanged-looking dining room does not remove a real cooking or equipment change, while a takeover does not itself prove every project needs the same plan route.

The purchase file should therefore return the new operator’s county application/issued evidence and the change-specific review decision. Old inspection history is useful for its actual purpose, not as a transferred permit. City zoning, building and fire requirements remain separate, and the inaccessible city material does not supply a verified fee, deadline or opening permission.

sections.heading: Keep the purchase decision connected to the missing evidence
paragraphs: Use the existing task allocation below to make clear who must obtain each answer. The amounts remain unverified rather than being treated as zero.

rows: Exact site, actual operator, ownership-change date and purchase conditions
Current and proposed menu, food processes, equipment and layout changes
Evaluation packet, menu where applicable, inspection result and any plan-review referral
City zoning/use/building/fire and landlord constraints; separate written answers
Separate evaluation, plan-review, construction and operating-permit estimates; amounts still unverified

sections.heading: Use old inspection records for the right purpose
paragraphs: SCCDineOut can help identify previous inspection observations and closure history. Match the facility and inspection date carefully. A prior score or placard is historical evidence; it does not transfer the permit or settle the buyer’s proposed menu.

Specialised processes listed in the packet, including reduced-oxygen packaging and manufacturing, need their own review.
