sections.heading: Keep a versioned record the team can revisit
paragraphs: For each offering, retain the document reference, issue and amendment dates, relevant addenda, and exact item or page supporting an entry. Record management duties and the definition of any reported outlet group beside the numbers. Keep the seller’s financial statements separate from outlet performance.

Finish by assigning each unresolved document or interpretation question to a responsible person before commitment. The comparison is a workspace for evidence and decisions. A completed spreadsheet, especially one populated automatically, does not establish that the documents have been fully reviewed or that the proposed model is permitted.

seoTitle: SCA service bids: wages, fringe benefits and labour costs
title: Federal service-contract bids: connect coverage, wages and delivery costs
description: Use the actual service solicitation, worker duties and wage/benefit terms before reusing a private-customer price; no coverage or rate is assumed.

sections.heading: First establish what kind of contract you are pricing
paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Labor’s Service Contract Act guidance concerns covered federal and District of Columbia service contracts performed through service employees, subject to exceptions. For covered contracts over $2,500, the applicable wage determination and fringe benefits matter. Coverage cannot be settled from the word “cleaning” or “maintenance” alone.

Identify the buyer, contract type, place of performance and work to be done. A private customer’s request for bids is not automatically a federal service contract. Equally, where you will work as a subcontractor, do not assume that the relevant contract obligations disappear because another business has the direct agreement with the government. The actual coverage, worker duties and exceptions need to be assessed.

sections.heading: Obtain the documents that turn a service description into a cost
paragraphs: Ask for the actual solicitation and its incorporated clauses, the relevant wage determination, job descriptions and work locations. Obtain any relevant facts about the predecessor contract and collective bargaining agreement. These are inputs to the coverage and cost review, rather than interchangeable background documents.

Map what workers will actually do to the relevant classifications in the contract materials. A general title such as “team member” may hide different duties. Use the applicable wage and benefit terms in the model; a generic national minimum wage or the brand’s existing rate overseas does not establish the cost of this particular covered work.

sections.heading: Distinguish legal obligations from the buyer’s other conditions
paragraphs: A buyer or prime contractor may also ask for insurance, registrations, financial capacity, references, security controls or reporting. Record where each requirement comes from: a sourced legal rule, an incorporated contract term or another procurement condition. That makes it easier to identify the responsible person and the evidence needed.

The distinction does not mean that a contractual condition can be ignored. It means the team should avoid describing every item in a bid pack as a generally applicable law. Put the document and clause next to each cost or task, and record any uncertainty that could change the promised service or price.

sections.heading: Fictional example: one supervisor, several cleaning sites
paragraphs: A fictional cleaning partner starts with its private-office bid template. It assumes one supervisor can cover several sites and budgets ordinary cleaner wages. The proposed government work has specific staffing periods, labour categories and reporting requirements. Without the applicable determination and actual duties, the old template cannot establish a reliable bid.

The bid lead obtains the contract materials, and the payroll lead maps jobs and benefits. The operations lead checks whether the supervisor can travel between sites while meeting the required coverage, and whether travel and reporting time have been included in the cost model. These are practical checks on the planned delivery arrangement; this example supplies no wage figure or staffing permission.

The finance lead then places wages, benefits and other start-up payments on the dates money will be needed, alongside the expected customer-payment dates. A price that eventually covers costs may still require cash before invoices are paid. If a material wage, benefit or staffing input remains unknown, record the bid as incomplete rather than treating the missing cost as zero.

sections.heading: Try the bid: which unsupported inputs prevent a reliable price?
paragraphs: Use the fictional cleaning partner bidding for several government sites. It has reused a private-office wage template and one-supervisor assumption, but lacks the applicable determination and full job/staffing evidence. Before reading the answer, separate the coverage, payroll, delivery and cash questions.

Answer: first identify the actual buyer, contract, performance location, worker duties and applicable exceptions. The reviewed SCA guidance concerns covered federal and District of Columbia service contracts through service employees; for covered contracts over $2,500, the applicable wage determination and fringe benefits matter. A service label alone decides neither coverage nor a wage. A subcontracting role also does not by itself remove relevant obligations.

The bid lead obtains the solicitation and incorporated terms; payroll maps actual jobs and applicable wages/benefits; operations checks required site coverage, travel and reporting; finance places the payments beside expected receipts. Mark a critical missing input as unresolved, not zero. Keep sourced legal duties, contract clauses and other buyer requirements identified separately so no procurement condition is presented as a law for every service business.

sections.heading: Produce a checklist that remains useful during delivery
paragraphs: Keep a solicitation-to-cost checklist owned jointly by the bid and payroll leads. Link each material labour assumption to the relevant document, job and work location. Coverage and applicable terms matter during performance as well as before the bid commitment.
bullets: Record the buyer, contract type, place of performance and proposed worker duties.
Identify the applicable coverage, exceptions and incorporated clauses.
Obtain the relevant wage determination and predecessor-contract facts.
Price the applicable wages, benefits, staffing periods and reporting work.
Test the dates of start-up payments against expected receipts.
Resolve critical unknowns before committing to a price.
